# Production environment variables
# Copy to .env on your production server and fill in the values.

# Generate with: python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(50))'
SECRET_KEY=<paste-a-50-character-key-here>
ENVIRONMENT=production
ALLOWED_HOSTS=yourdomain.com,www.yourdomain.com
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://yourdomain.com,https://www.yourdomain.com
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL=no-reply@yourdomain.com
# DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE is read before this file, so setting it here has no effect.
# Export it in the server's environment instead:
#   export DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=my_shop.settings.production

SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT=True
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS=31536000
# Turn these on only once every subdomain serves HTTPS; preload is hard to undo.
SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS=False
SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD=False
# Only enable behind a proxy that strips a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto.
TRUST_PROXY_SSL_HEADER=False

DB_NAME=my_shop
DB_USER=django_user
DB_PASSWORD=<set-password>
DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
DB_PORT=3306

==> README.md (0644)
# my-shop

Generated by [django-stack](https://github.com/vaibdix/django-stack).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.13 or newer
- Docker, for the MySQL container

## Setup

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
[ -f .env ] || cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d --wait db
.venv/bin/python manage.py migrate
.venv/bin/python manage.py createsuperuser
.venv/bin/python manage.py runserver
```

No superuser is created for you. Run `createsuperuser` above, then sign in at
`/admin/`. On Windows the interpreter is `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`.

`.env.example` ships a placeholder `SECRET_KEY` so the project boots immediately.
Replace it before you deploy anything:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(50))'
```

## Environment

`ENVIRONMENT` is the only switch for `DEBUG`. Set it to `local`, `test`, `staging`
or `production`; `DEBUG` is on for `local` and `test`. Everything that behaves differently in development — the browsable
API, plain-text logging, the browser-reload endpoint — reads that one value.

Configuration is validated at startup by `my_shop/conf.py`.
A missing or malformed variable stops the process with a message naming the field
rather than failing later at the point of use.

## Configuration

`.env.example` lists what every environment needs. The variables below are
optional; set them in `.env` or in the process environment when you need them.

Email, read in staging and production:

| Variable | Example |
|----------|---------|
| `EMAIL_HOST` | `smtp.gmail.com` |
| `EMAIL_PORT` | `587` |
| `EMAIL_USE_TLS` | `True` |
| `EMAIL_HOST_USER` | |
| `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD` | |
| `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL` | `no-reply@yourdomain.com`; production refuses Django's `webmaster@localhost` |

Production security, read in staging and production:

| Variable | Example |
|----------|---------|
| `ADMIN_URL` | `admin/` |
| `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` | `https://example.com` |
| `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` | `True` |
| `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS` | `31536000` |
| `SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` | `False` |
| `SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD` | `False` |
| `TRUST_PROXY_SSL_HEADER` | `False` |

Error tracking with Sentry, off until `SENTRY_DSN` is set:

| Variable | Example |
|----------|---------|
| `SENTRY_DSN` | the DSN of your Sentry project |
| `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` | defaults to `ENVIRONMENT`; set it only to report under another name |
| `SENTRY_RELEASE` | |
| `SENTRY_SEND_PII` | `False` |
| `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` | `0.1` |
| `SENTRY_PROFILE_SESSION_SAMPLE_RATE` | `0.1` |

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python manage.py test --settings=my_shop.settings.test
```

The suite needs no `.env`, so it runs the same in a fresh clone and in CI: `settings.test` sets `ENVIRONMENT=test`, which supplies a throwaway `SECRET_KEY` that no other environment accepts. The database settings (`DB_*`) still have to point at a running MySQL.

## Linting and types

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
.venv/bin/python -m ruff format .
.venv/bin/python -m mypy .
.venv/bin/python -m djlint . --check
```

mypy loads `settings.test`, which sets `ENVIRONMENT=test`, so it
needs no `.env` either. It reads the `DB_*` settings as the tests do, but never connects.

`.venv/bin/python -m pre-commit run --all-files` runs all of the above as a gate.

## Deployment

```bash
export DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=my_shop.settings.production
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python manage.py migrate --noinput
.venv/bin/python manage.py createcachetable
.venv/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput
.venv/bin/python manage.py check --deploy
.venv/bin/python -m gunicorn my_shop.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000
```

Static files are served by WhiteNoise, so no separate web server is required for
them. `check --deploy` warns that HSTS covers neither subdomains nor the preload
list: set `SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` and `SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD` to `True` once
every subdomain serves HTTPS, because leaving the preload list takes months. Set
`TRUST_PROXY_SSL_HEADER=True` only behind a proxy that overwrites
`X-Forwarded-Proto`. Set `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL` to an address your mail server
sends from: production refuses Django's default, `webmaster@localhost`. Copy `.env.production.example` to `.env` on the server and fill it in.

`manage.py` defaults to `settings.local` and gunicorn to `settings.production`. Export
`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` before running management commands on a server: it is read before
`.env`, so it has no effect there. `settings.local` refuses to start unless `ENVIRONMENT=local`,
and `settings.production` refuses to start with it.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|------|------------------|
| `my_shop/` | settings, URLs, WSGI/ASGI and the health check |
| `my_shop/settings/` | `base.py`, `local.py`, `production.py`, `test.py` |
| `catalog/models.py` | the model, its queryset and its database constraints |
| `catalog/fields.py` | the ISBN field and the rules every write path (forms, admin, API) shares |
| `catalog/api/` | the Ninja API, its router and schemas |
| `catalog/templates/` | the pages for this app |
| `templates/` | base layout, home page and error pages |
| `static/` | CSS and JavaScript |

## Endpoints

| URL | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `/` | Home |
| `/admin/` | Django admin |
| `/healthz/` | Health check, including the database. Served over plain HTTP too, so a load balancer can probe it; the probe must send a `Host` that is in `ALLOWED_HOSTS` |
| `/api/v1/books` | Books: `GET` to list (`?search=`), `POST` to create |
| `/api/v1/books/{id}` | One book: `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` |
| `/api/v1/books/recent` | Books added recently |
| `/api/v1/docs` | Interactive API documentation |
| `/api/v1/openapi.json` | OpenAPI schema |
| `/accounts/login/` | Sign in |
| `/accounts/signup/` | Create an account |

## API access

The API is read-only for anonymous callers: `GET` works without signing in, and
writes need an authenticated user. Writes use Django session authentication and answer 401 until you sign in
at the admin. To make the demo API writable without signing in, remove
`auth=django_auth` from the write operations in `catalog/api/router.py`.
==> WELCOME.md (0644)
# Welcome to Your Django Project!

## Getting Started

- The `Workspace: Start Dev` task starts the Django server in an integrated terminal.
- VS Code asks once whether to allow automatic tasks for this folder. Allow it to start the task on open, or run `Workspace: Start Dev` from the Tasks menu.

## Dev Startup Scripts
- `start-dev.sh` (macOS and Linux) and `start-dev.bat` (Windows) open this folder in a new VS Code window.
- Both need the `code` command on your PATH.

## Admin Setup
- `README.md` explains how to create a Django superuser.

## Project Structure
- `manage.py` - Django management script
- `templates/` - HTML templates
- `static/` - Static files
- `my_shop/` - Django project configuration

from django.contrib.auth.admin import UserAdmin as BaseUserAdmin

from .models import User


@admin.register(User)
class UserAdmin(BaseUserAdmin[User]):
    add_fieldsets = (
        (
            None,
            {
                "classes": ("wide",),
                "fields": ("username", "email", "usable_password", "password1", "password2"),
            },
        ),
    )
    list_display = ("username", "email", "is_staff", "is_active", "date_joined")
    list_filter = ("is_staff", "is_superuser", "is_active")
    search_fields = ("username", "email", "first_name", "last_name")
    ordering = ("-date_joined",)

==> accounts/models.py (0644)
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models
from django.db.models.functions import Lower


class User(AbstractUser):
    email = models.EmailField()

    class Meta(AbstractUser.Meta):
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(
                Lower("email"),
                name="accounts_user_email_ci_unique",
                violation_error_message="A user with this email address already exists.",
            ),
        ]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.get_username()
==> accounts/tests.py (0644)
import re

from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core import mail
from django.db import IntegrityError
from django.db import transaction
from django.test import TestCase
from django.test import override_settings
from django.urls import reverse

TEST_PASSWORD = "not-a-real-password"  # noqa: S105


class UserModelTests(TestCase):
    def test_the_project_uses_its_own_user_model(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(get_user_model()._meta.label, "accounts.User")

    def test_email_is_unique(self) -> None:
        model = get_user_model()
        model.objects.create_user(username="first", email="taken@example.com", password=TEST_PASSWORD)

        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():
            model.objects.create_user(username="second", email="taken@example.com", password=TEST_PASSWORD)

    def test_email_is_unique_whatever_its_case(self) -> None:
        model = get_user_model()
        model.objects.create_user(username="first", email="Taken@Example.com", password=TEST_PASSWORD)

        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():
            model.objects.create_user(username="second", email="taken@example.com", password=TEST_PASSWORD)


class AdminAddUserTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        admin_user = get_user_model().objects.create_superuser(
            username="admin",
            email="admin@example.com",
            password=TEST_PASSWORD,
        )
        self.client.force_login(admin_user)

    def test_adding_a_user_saves_the_email(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("admin:accounts_user_add"),
            {"username": "newcomer", "email": "newcomer@example.com", "usable_password": "false"},
        )

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertEqual(get_user_model().objects.get(username="newcomer").email, "newcomer@example.com")

    def test_adding_a_user_with_a_taken_email_is_refused_whatever_its_case(self) -> None:
        get_user_model().objects.create_user(username="first", email="Taken@Example.com", password=TEST_PASSWORD)

        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("admin:accounts_user_add"),
            {"username": "second", "email": "taken@example.com", "usable_password": "false"},
        )

        self.assertContains(response, "A user with this email address already exists.")
        self.assertFalse(get_user_model().objects.filter(username="second").exists())


@override_settings(ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION="mandatory")
class EmailConfirmationTests(TestCase):
    def test_a_new_account_is_confirmed_from_the_emailed_page(self) -> None:
        self.client.post(
            reverse("account_signup"),
            {
                "email": "reader@example.com",
                "username": "reader",
                "password1": TEST_PASSWORD,
                "password2": TEST_PASSWORD,
            },
        )
        key = re.search(r"/confirm-email/([^/\s]+)/", str(mail.outbox[0].body))
        assert key is not None

        page = self.client.get(reverse("account_confirm_email", args=[key.group(1)]))
        form = re.search(r'<form method="post"\s+action="([^"]+)"', page.content.decode())
        assert form is not None, "the confirmation page has no form to confirm with"

        self.client.post(form.group(1))
        self.assertTrue(EmailAddress.objects.get(email="reader@example.com").verified)


class PasswordResetFromKeyTests(TestCase):
    def test_a_spent_reset_link_says_so_instead_of_showing_the_form(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("account_reset_password_from_key", kwargs={"uidb36": "0", "key": "spent-key"}),
        )

        self.assertContains(response, "This link no longer works")
        self.assertNotContains(response, "Save password")

    search_fields = ("title", "author", "isbn")
    list_filter = ("publication_date", "created_at", "updated_at")
    ordering = ("-created_at",)
    readonly_fields = ("created_at", "updated_at")

==> catalog/api/api.py (0644)
from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.http import HttpRequest
from django.http import HttpResponse
from ninja import NinjaAPI
from ninja.throttling import AnonRateThrottle
from ninja.throttling import AuthRateThrottle

from catalog.api.router import router

api = NinjaAPI(
    title="my-shop API",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="API documentation for my-shop",
    urls_namespace="api",
    throttle=[
        AnonRateThrottle("100/h"),
        AuthRateThrottle("1000/h"),
    ],
)

api.add_router("/books", router)


@api.exception_handler(ValidationError)
def model_validation_failed(request: HttpRequest, exc: ValidationError) -> HttpResponse:
    return api.create_response(request, {"detail": exc.message_dict}, status=422)
==> catalog/api/router.py (0644)
from django.http import HttpRequest
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from ninja import Router
from ninja import Status
from ninja.pagination import PageNumberPagination
from ninja.pagination import paginate
from ninja.security import django_auth

from catalog.api.schemas import BookIn
from catalog.api.schemas import BookOut
from catalog.models import Book
from catalog.models import BookQuerySet

PAGE_SIZE = 20

router = Router(tags=["books"])


@router.get("", response=list[BookOut])
@paginate(PageNumberPagination, page_size=PAGE_SIZE)
def list_books(request: HttpRequest, search: str = "") -> BookQuerySet:
    return Book.objects.search(search)


@router.get("/recent", response=list[BookOut])
@paginate(PageNumberPagination, page_size=PAGE_SIZE)
def recent_books(request: HttpRequest, search: str = "") -> BookQuerySet:
    return Book.objects.search(search).recent()


@router.get("/{int:book_id}", response=BookOut)
def get_book(request: HttpRequest, book_id: int) -> Book:
    return get_object_or_404(Book, pk=book_id)


def validated_save(book: Book) -> Book:
    book.full_clean()
    book.save()
    return book


@router.post("", response={201: BookOut}, auth=django_auth)
def create_book(request: HttpRequest, payload: BookIn) -> Status[Book]:
    return Status(201, validated_save(Book(**payload.model_dump())))


@router.put("/{int:book_id}", response=BookOut, auth=django_auth)
def update_book(request: HttpRequest, book_id: int, payload: BookIn) -> Book:
    book = get_object_or_404(Book, pk=book_id)
    for field, value in payload.model_dump().items():
        setattr(book, field, value)
    return validated_save(book)


@router.delete("/{int:book_id}", response={204: None}, auth=django_auth)
def delete_book(request: HttpRequest, book_id: int) -> Status[None]:
    get_object_or_404(Book, pk=book_id).delete()
    return Status(204, None)

==> catalog/fields.py (0644)
from datetime import date

from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.core.validators import RegexValidator
from django.db import models
from django.utils import timezone

ISBN_INPUT_MAX_LENGTH = 17

ISBN_VALIDATOR = RegexValidator(r"^\d{13}$", "ISBN must be exactly 13 digits, with or without hyphens.")


def normalise_isbn(value: str) -> str:
    return value.replace("-", "").replace(" ", "")


def validate_not_in_future(value: date) -> None:
    if value > timezone.localdate():
        message = "A book cannot be published in the future."
        raise ValidationError(message, code="future_date")


class ISBNField(models.CharField[str, str]):
    description = "An ISBN-13, stored as 13 digits and accepted with hyphens or spaces"

    def to_python(self, value: object) -> str | None:
        text = super().to_python(value)
        return normalise_isbn(text) if text else text

    def get_prep_value(self, value: object) -> object:
        prepared = super().get_prep_value(value)
        return normalise_isbn(prepared) if isinstance(prepared, str) else prepared

    def pre_save(self, model_instance: models.Model, add: bool) -> object:
        value = super().pre_save(model_instance, add)
        if isinstance(value, str):
            value = normalise_isbn(value)
            setattr(model_instance, self.attname, value)
        return value

            "price": forms.NumberInput(attrs={"class": INPUT_CLASS, "placeholder": "24.99", "step": "0.01"}),
        }
==> catalog/htmx.py (0644)
from typing import cast

from django.http import HttpRequest as HttpRequestBase
from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.utils.cache import patch_vary_headers
from django.views.generic.base import TemplateResponseMixin
from django_htmx.middleware import HtmxDetails

FRAGMENT_HEADERS = ("HX-Request", "HX-Boosted", "HX-History-Restore-Request")


class HtmxHttpRequest(HttpRequestBase):
    htmx: HtmxDetails


def wants_fragment(request: HttpRequestBase) -> bool:
    htmx = cast("HtmxHttpRequest", request).htmx
    return bool(htmx) and not htmx.boosted and not htmx.history_restore_request


class HtmxTemplateMixin(TemplateResponseMixin):
    fragment_template_name: str

    request: HttpRequestBase

    def get_template_names(self) -> list[str]:
        if wants_fragment(self.request):
            return [self.fragment_template_name]
        return super().get_template_names()

    def render_to_response(self, context: dict[str, object], **response_kwargs: object) -> HttpResponse:
        response = super().render_to_response(context, **response_kwargs)
        patch_vary_headers(response, FRAGMENT_HEADERS)
        return response

==> catalog/management/commands/create_sample_data.py (0644)
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import TypedDict

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

from catalog.models import Book


class BookSeed(TypedDict):
    title: str
    author: str
    isbn: str
    publication_date: date
    price: Decimal


BOOKS: list[BookSeed] = [
    {
        "title": "Django for Beginners",
        "author": "William Vincent",
        "isbn": "9781735467200",
        "publication_date": date(2022, 1, 1),
        "price": Decimal("39.99"),
    },
    {
        "title": "Two Scoops of Django",
        "author": "Daniel Roy Greenfeld",
        "isbn": "9780692915738",
        "publication_date": date(2021, 5, 15),
        "price": Decimal("49.99"),
    },
]


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Creates sample book data"

    def handle(self, *args: str, **options: object) -> None:
        Book.objects.bulk_create(
            [Book(**book) for book in BOOKS],
            update_conflicts=True,
            update_fields=["title", "author", "publication_date", "price"],
        )

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(f"Seeded {len(BOOKS)} books."))

==> catalog/models.py (0644)
from datetime import date
from datetime import timedelta

from django.core.validators import MinValueValidator
from django.db import models
from django.db.models import Q
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils import timezone

from core.models import TimeStampedModel

from .fields import ISBN_INPUT_MAX_LENGTH
from .fields import ISBN_VALIDATOR
from .fields import ISBNField
from .fields import normalise_isbn
from .fields import validate_not_in_future

RECENT_WINDOW_DAYS = 30

EARLIEST_PUBLICATION_DATE = date(1450, 1, 1)

PUBLICATION_DATE_TOO_EARLY = "A book cannot be published before 1450."

NEGATIVE_PRICE = "A price cannot be negative."


class BookQuerySet(models.QuerySet["Book"]):
    def search(self, term: str) -> "BookQuerySet":
        cleaned = term.strip()
        if not cleaned:
            return self
        return self.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=cleaned) | Q(author__icontains=cleaned) | Q(isbn__icontains=normalise_isbn(cleaned)),
        )

    def recent(self, days: int = RECENT_WINDOW_DAYS) -> "BookQuerySet":
        return self.filter(created_at__gte=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=days))


class Book(TimeStampedModel):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200, help_text="The full title, as printed on the cover.")
    author = models.CharField(max_length=100, help_text="Primary author. One name per book in this example.")
    isbn = ISBNField(
        max_length=ISBN_INPUT_MAX_LENGTH,
        unique=True,
        validators=[ISBN_VALIDATOR],
        help_text="Thirteen digits. Hyphens and spaces are accepted and removed.",
    )
    publication_date = models.DateField(
        validators=[MinValueValidator(EARLIEST_PUBLICATION_DATE, PUBLICATION_DATE_TOO_EARLY), validate_not_in_future],
        help_text="The date this edition was published. Never in the future.",
    )
    price = models.DecimalField(
        max_digits=10,
        decimal_places=2,
        validators=[MinValueValidator(0, NEGATIVE_PRICE)],
        help_text="Retail price. Never negative.",
    )
    objects = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

    class Meta:
        ordering = ("-created_at", "-pk")
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=("-created_at", "-id"))]
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=Q(price__gte=0),
                name="book_price_not_negative",
                violation_error_message=NEGATIVE_PRICE,
            ),
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=Q(publication_date__gte=EARLIEST_PUBLICATION_DATE),
                name="book_publication_date_plausible",
                violation_error_message=PUBLICATION_DATE_TOO_EARLY,
            ),
        ]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.title

    def get_absolute_url(self) -> str:
        return reverse("catalog:book_edit", args=(self.pk,))

==> catalog/tests/test_api.py (0644)
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from catalog.models import Book

TEST_PASSWORD = "not-a-real-password"  # noqa: S105

NEW_BOOK = {
    "title": "Architecture Patterns with Python",
    "author": "Harry Percival",
    "isbn": "9781492052203",
    "publication_date": "2020-03-05",
    "price": "54.99",
}


class CatalogAPITests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.book = Book.objects.create(
            title="Fluent Python",
            author="Luciano Ramalho",
            isbn="9781492056355",
            publication_date=date(2022, 4, 1),
            price=Decimal("64.99"),
        )

    def sign_in(self) -> None:
        user = get_user_model().objects.create_user(username="editor", password=TEST_PASSWORD)
        self.client.force_login(user)

    def test_anonymous_callers_can_read(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("api:list_books"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()["count"], 1)

    def test_a_single_book_is_found_by_id(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("api:get_book", args=[self.book.pk]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()["isbn"], "9781492056355")

        response = self.client.get(reverse("api:get_book", args=[self.book.pk + 1000]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

    def test_anonymous_callers_cannot_write(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.post(reverse("api:create_book"), NEW_BOOK, content_type="application/json")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 401)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn=NEW_BOOK["isbn"]).exists())

    def test_authenticated_callers_can_create(self) -> None:
        self.sign_in()
        response = self.client.post(reverse("api:create_book"), NEW_BOOK, content_type="application/json")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 201)
        self.assertTrue(Book.objects.filter(isbn=NEW_BOOK["isbn"]).exists())

    def test_authenticated_callers_can_delete(self) -> None:
        self.sign_in()
        response = self.client.delete(reverse("api:delete_book", args=[self.book.pk]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 204)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(pk=self.book.pk).exists())

    def test_recent_books_are_routed(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("api:recent_books"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()["count"], 1)

    def test_search_matches_title_author_and_isbn(self) -> None:
        for term in ("fluent", "ramalho", "9781492"):
            response = self.client.get(reverse("api:list_books"), {"search": term})
            self.assertEqual(response.json()["count"], 1, term)

        response = self.client.get(reverse("api:list_books"), {"search": "nothing matches this"})
        self.assertEqual(response.json()["count"], 0)

    def test_a_hyphenated_isbn_is_normalised(self) -> None:
        self.sign_in()
        payload = {**NEW_BOOK, "isbn": "978-1-2345-6789-7"}
        response = self.client.post(reverse("api:create_book"), payload, content_type="application/json")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()["isbn"], "9781234567897")

    def test_a_book_cannot_be_published_in_the_future(self) -> None:
        self.sign_in()
        payload = {**NEW_BOOK, "publication_date": "2999-01-01"}
        response = self.client.post(reverse("api:create_book"), payload, content_type="application/json")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 422)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn=NEW_BOOK["isbn"]).exists())

    def test_a_book_cannot_predate_printing(self) -> None:
        self.sign_in()
        payload = {**NEW_BOOK, "publication_date": "1400-01-01"}
        response = self.client.post(reverse("api:create_book"), payload, content_type="application/json")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 422)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn=NEW_BOOK["isbn"]).exists())
==> catalog/tests/test_models.py (0644)
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from django.db import IntegrityError
from django.test import TestCase

from catalog.models import Book


class CatalogModelTests(TestCase):
    def test_str_is_the_title(self) -> None:
        book = Book.objects.create(
            title="The Pragmatic Programmer",
            author="Andy Hunt",
            isbn="9780135957059",
            publication_date=date(2019, 9, 13),
            price=Decimal("44.99"),
        )
        self.assertEqual(str(book), "The Pragmatic Programmer")

    def test_newest_book_comes_first(self) -> None:
        older = Book.objects.create(
            title="Older",
            author="A",
            isbn="1111111111111",
            publication_date=date(2020, 1, 1),
            price=Decimal("10.00"),
        )
        newer = Book.objects.create(
            title="Newer",
            author="B",
            isbn="2222222222222",
            publication_date=date(2021, 1, 1),
            price=Decimal("20.00"),
        )
        self.assertEqual(list(Book.objects.all()), [newer, older])

    def test_search_matches_title_author_and_isbn(self) -> None:
        book = Book.objects.create(
            title="Fluent Python",
            author="Luciano Ramalho",
            isbn="9781492056355",
            publication_date=date(2022, 4, 1),
            price=Decimal("64.99"),
        )
        for term in ("fluent", "ramalho", "9781492"):
            self.assertEqual(list(Book.objects.search(term)), [book], term)
        self.assertEqual(list(Book.objects.search("nothing matches this")), [])

    def test_a_saved_isbn_is_normalised_on_the_instance_too(self) -> None:
        book = Book.objects.create(
            title="Fluent Python",
            author="Luciano Ramalho",
            isbn="978-1-4920-5635-5",
            publication_date=date(2022, 4, 1),
            price=Decimal("64.99"),
        )
        self.assertEqual(book.isbn, "9781492056355")
        self.assertEqual(list(Book.objects.search("978-1-4920-5635-5")), [book])

    def test_the_database_rejects_a_negative_price(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            Book.objects.create(
                title="Free Money",
                author="Nobody",
                isbn="3333333333333",

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from catalog.models import Book

TEST_PASSWORD = "not-a-real-password"  # noqa: S105

NEW_BOOK = {
    "title": "Architecture Patterns with Python",
    "author": "Harry Percival",
    "isbn": "9781492052203",
    "publication_date": "2020-03-05",
    "price": "54.99",
}


class CatalogViewTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.book = Book.objects.create(
            title="Fluent Python",
            author="Luciano Ramalho",
            isbn="9781492056355",
            publication_date=date(2022, 4, 1),
            price=Decimal("64.99"),
        )
        self.user = get_user_model().objects.create_user(username="editor", password=TEST_PASSWORD)

    def test_list_shows_existing_books(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("catalog:book_list"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(response, "Fluent Python")

    def test_search_narrows_the_list(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("catalog:book_list"), {"q": "ramalho"})
        self.assertContains(response, "Fluent Python")

        response = self.client.get(reverse("catalog:book_list"), {"q": "no such book"})
        self.assertNotContains(response, "Fluent Python")

    def test_create_adds_a_book(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(reverse("catalog:book_create"), NEW_BOOK)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertTrue(Book.objects.filter(isbn="9781492052203").exists())

    def test_delete_removes_a_book(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(reverse("catalog:book_delete", args=[self.book.pk]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(pk=self.book.pk).exists())

    def test_anonymous_visitors_cannot_write(self) -> None:
        writes: tuple[tuple[str, dict[str, str]], ...] = (
            (reverse("catalog:book_create"), NEW_BOOK),
            (reverse("catalog:book_edit", args=[self.book.pk]), NEW_BOOK),
            (reverse("catalog:book_delete", args=[self.book.pk]), {}),
        )
        for url, payload in writes:
            response = self.client.post(url, payload)
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 302, url)
            self.assertIn("login", response["Location"], url)

        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn="9781492052203").exists())
        self.assertTrue(Book.objects.filter(pk=self.book.pk).exists())

    def test_an_invalid_submission_says_why(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("catalog:book_create"),
            {**NEW_BOOK, "isbn": "not-an-isbn"},
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "ISBN must be exactly 13 digits, with or without hyphens.", status_code=200)

    def test_a_hyphenated_isbn_is_normalised(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        self.client.post(reverse("catalog:book_create"), {**NEW_BOOK, "isbn": "978-1-4920-5220-3"})
        self.assertTrue(Book.objects.filter(isbn="9781492052203").exists())

    def test_a_book_cannot_be_published_in_the_future(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("catalog:book_create"),
            {**NEW_BOOK, "publication_date": "2999-01-01"},
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "A book cannot be published in the future.", status_code=200)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn="9781492052203").exists())

    def test_a_book_cannot_predate_printing(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("catalog:book_create"),
            {**NEW_BOOK, "publication_date": "1400-01-01"},
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "A book cannot be published before 1450.", status_code=200)
        self.assertFalse(Book.objects.filter(isbn="9781492052203").exists())

    def test_an_htmx_search_gets_only_the_list(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("catalog:book_list"), {"q": "ramalho"}, headers={"HX-Request": "true"})
        self.assertContains(response, "Fluent Python")
        self.assertNotContains(response, "<html")

    def test_a_history_restore_gets_the_full_page(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(
            reverse("catalog:book_list"),
            {"q": "ramalho"},
            headers={"HX-Request": "true", "HX-History-Restore-Request": "true"},
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "<html")

    def test_the_list_tells_caches_it_varies_with_htmx(self) -> None:
        response = self.client.get(reverse("catalog:book_list"))
        vary = {header.strip() for header in response["Vary"].split(",")}
        self.assertLessEqual({"HX-Request", "HX-Boosted", "HX-History-Restore-Request"}, vary)

    def test_an_htmx_submission_hands_the_redirect_to_the_browser(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(reverse("catalog:book_create"), NEW_BOOK, headers={"HX-Request": "true"})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 204)
        self.assertEqual(response["HX-Redirect"], reverse("catalog:book_list"))

    def test_an_invalid_htmx_submission_returns_only_the_form(self) -> None:
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        response = self.client.post(
            reverse("catalog:book_create"),
            {**NEW_BOOK, "isbn": "not-an-isbn"},
            headers={"HX-Request": "true"},
        )
        self.assertContains(response, "ISBN must be exactly 13 digits", status_code=422)
        self.assertNotContains(response, "<html", status_code=422)

from http import HTTPStatus

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.mixins import LoginRequiredMixin
from django.contrib.messages.views import SuccessMessageMixin
from django.forms import Form
from django.http import HttpRequest
from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.urls import reverse_lazy
from django.views.generic import CreateView
from django.views.generic import DeleteView
from django.views.generic import ListView
from django.views.generic import UpdateView
from django.views.generic.edit import ModelFormMixin

from .forms import BookForm
from .htmx import HtmxTemplateMixin
from .htmx import wants_fragment
from .models import Book
from .models import BookQuerySet

SEARCH_PARAM = "q"

PAGE_SIZE = 12

LIST_URL = reverse_lazy("catalog:book_list")

LIST_TEMPLATE = "catalog/book_list.html"
FORM_TEMPLATE = "catalog/book_form.html"
DELETE_TEMPLATE = "catalog/book_delete.html"
LIST_ITEMS_TEMPLATE = "catalog/partials/book_list_items.html"
FORM_PARTIAL_TEMPLATE = "catalog/partials/book_form_partial.html"


class BookListView(HtmxTemplateMixin, ListView[Book]):
    context_object_name = "books"
    paginate_by = PAGE_SIZE
    template_name = LIST_TEMPLATE
    fragment_template_name = LIST_ITEMS_TEMPLATE

    def setup(self, request: HttpRequest, *args: object, **kwargs: object) -> None:
        super().setup(request, *args, **kwargs)
        self.extra_context = {"query": self.search_term}

    def get_queryset(self) -> BookQuerySet:
        return Book.objects.search(self.search_term)

    @property
    def search_term(self) -> str:
        return self.request.GET.get(SEARCH_PARAM, "")


class BookFormMixin(
    LoginRequiredMixin,
    HtmxTemplateMixin,
    SuccessMessageMixin[BookForm],
    ModelFormMixin[Book, BookForm],
):
    model = Book
    form_class = BookForm
    success_url = LIST_URL
    template_name: str | None = FORM_TEMPLATE
    fragment_template_name = FORM_PARTIAL_TEMPLATE

    def form_valid(self, form: BookForm) -> HttpResponse:
        response = super().form_valid(form)
        if wants_fragment(self.request):
            return hand_back_to_the_browser(response["Location"])
        return response

    def form_invalid(self, form: BookForm) -> HttpResponse:
        response = super().form_invalid(form)
        if wants_fragment(self.request):
            response.status_code = HTTPStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY
        return response


class BookCreateView(BookFormMixin, CreateView[Book, BookForm]):
    extra_context = {"action": "Create"}
    success_message = "Book created successfully!"


class BookUpdateView(BookFormMixin, UpdateView[Book, BookForm]):
    extra_context = {"action": "Edit"}
    success_message = "Book updated successfully!"


class BookDeleteView(LoginRequiredMixin, DeleteView[Book, Form]):
    model = Book
    success_url = LIST_URL
    template_name = DELETE_TEMPLATE

    def form_valid(self, form: Form) -> HttpResponse:
        deleted = super().form_valid(form)
        if wants_fragment(self.request):
            return HttpResponse("")
        messages.success(self.request, "Book deleted successfully!")
        return deleted


def hand_back_to_the_browser(url: str) -> HttpResponse:
    response = HttpResponse(status=HTTPStatus.NO_CONTENT)
    response["HX-Redirect"] = url
    return response

    class Meta:
        abstract = True
        get_latest_by = "created_at"

==> manage.py (0755)
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Django's command-line utility for administrative tasks."""

import os
import sys


def main() -> None:
    """Run administrative tasks."""
    os.environ.setdefault("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "my_shop.settings.local")
    try:
        from django.core.management import execute_from_command_line
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(
            "Couldn't import Django. Are you sure it's installed and "
            "available on your PYTHONPATH environment variable? Did you "
            "forget to activate a virtual environment?"
        ) from exc
    execute_from_command_line(sys.argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated
from typing import Literal

from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from pydantic import BeforeValidator
from pydantic import Field
from pydantic import SecretStr
from pydantic import ValidationError
from pydantic import model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
from pydantic_settings import NoDecode
from pydantic_settings import SettingsConfigDict

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def _split_comma(value: object) -> object:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
    return value


CommaSeparated = Annotated[list[str], NoDecode, BeforeValidator(_split_comma)]

Environment = Literal["local", "test", "staging", "production"]

Port = Annotated[int, Field(ge=1, le=65535)]
SampleRate = Annotated[float, Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)]

SecretKey = Annotated[SecretStr, Field(min_length=50)]

EMPTY_SECRET = SecretStr("")

TEST_SECRET_KEY = "insecure-test-only-key-used-when-environment-is-test-and-nowhere-else"  # noqa: S105


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=BASE_DIR / ".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    ENVIRONMENT: Environment = "production"

    ADMIN_URL: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, pattern=r"^[\w\-/]+/$")] = "admin/"

    SECRET_KEY: SecretKey
    ALLOWED_HOSTS: CommaSeparated = ["localhost", "127.0.0.1"]

    DB_NAME: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1)]
    DB_USER: str = "django_user"
    DB_PASSWORD: SecretStr = EMPTY_SECRET
    DB_HOST: str = "127.0.0.1"
    DB_PORT: Port = 3306
    DB_CONN_MAX_AGE: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)] = 60

    SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT: bool = True
    SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)] = 31536000
    SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS: bool = False
    SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD: bool = False
    TRUST_PROXY_SSL_HEADER: bool = False
    CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS: CommaSeparated = []

    EMAIL_HOST: str = "localhost"
    EMAIL_PORT: Port = 587
    EMAIL_HOST_USER: str = ""
    EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD: SecretStr = EMPTY_SECRET
    EMAIL_USE_TLS: bool = True
    DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL: str = "webmaster@localhost"

    SENTRY_DSN: SecretStr = EMPTY_SECRET
    SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT: str = ""
    SENTRY_RELEASE: str = ""
    SENTRY_SEND_PII: bool = False
    SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE: SampleRate = 0.0
    SENTRY_PROFILE_SESSION_SAMPLE_RATE: SampleRate = 0.0

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def default_the_secret_key_under_test(cls, data: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("ENVIRONMENT") == "test":
            data.setdefault("SECRET_KEY", TEST_SECRET_KEY)
        return data

    @property
    def DEBUG(self) -> bool:
        return self.ENVIRONMENT in {"local", "test"}


try:
    env = Settings()
except ValidationError as error:
    message = f"Invalid environment configuration:\n{error}"
    raise ImproperlyConfigured(message) from error

from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured

from .base import *  # noqa: F401,F403

if ENVIRONMENT != "local":
    message = (
        f"settings.local refuses to run with ENVIRONMENT={ENVIRONMENT}. manage.py picks settings.local "
        "unless DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE is exported, and .env is read too late to change that: "
        "export DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=my_shop.settings.production on the server."
    )
    raise ImproperlyConfigured(message)

ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["localhost", "127.0.0.1"]

INSTALLED_APPS = [*INSTALLED_APPS, "django_browser_reload"]

MIDDLEWARE = [*MIDDLEWARE, "django_browser_reload.middleware.BrowserReloadMiddleware"]

from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured

from . import base
from .base import *  # noqa: F401,F403

if ENVIRONMENT == "local":
    message = "settings.production refuses to run with ENVIRONMENT=local; set it to staging or production."
    raise ImproperlyConfigured(message)

if SECRET_KEY == "replace-this-placeholder-with-a-generated-50-char-key":  # noqa: S105
    message = "SECRET_KEY is still the .env.example placeholder; generate a real one before deploying."
    raise ImproperlyConfigured(message)

CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True

    path("", views.HomeView.as_view(), name="home"),
    path(settings.ADMIN_URL, admin.site.urls),
    path("healthz/", views.healthz, name="healthz"),
    path("accounts/", include("allauth.urls")),
    path("api/v1/", api.urls),
    path("catalog/", include("catalog.urls")),

==> my_shop/views.py (0644)
from django.db import Error
from django.db import connection
from django.http import HttpRequest
from django.http import JsonResponse
from django.views.generic import TemplateView


class HomeView(TemplateView):
    template_name = "index.html"


def healthz(request: HttpRequest) -> JsonResponse:
    try:
        connection.ensure_connection()
    except Error:
        return JsonResponse({"status": "error", "database": "unreachable"}, status=503)
    return JsonResponse({"status": "ok", "database": "ok"})

==> start-dev.bat (0644)
@echo off
setlocal
set "PROJECT_DIR=%~dp0"

where code >nul 2>&1
if %ERRORLEVEL% EQU 0 (
    start "" code -n "%PROJECT_DIR%."
    echo VS Code opened in a new window.
    echo Allow automatic tasks when VS Code asks, or run "Workspace: Start Dev" from the Tasks menu.
    echo Watch the Django terminal inside VS Code.
) else (
    echo The code command is not on your PATH. Open this folder in VS Code yourself.
)
echo Open http://localhost:8000 once the server is ready.
==> start-dev.sh (0755)
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

if command -v code >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  code -n "$SCRIPT_DIR" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  echo "VS Code opened in a new window."
  echo "Allow automatic tasks when VS Code asks, or run 'Workspace: Start Dev' from the Tasks menu."
  echo "Watch the Django terminal inside VS Code."
else
  echo "The 'code' command is not on your PATH."
  echo "In VS Code, run 'Shell Command: Install code command in PATH', or open this folder yourself."
fi
echo "Open http://localhost:8000 once the server is ready."

==> static/js/main.js (0644)
document.body.addEventListener("htmx:beforeSwap", function (event) {
    if (event.detail.xhr.status === 422) {
        event.detail.shouldSwap = true;
        event.detail.isError = false;
    }
});
